chapter: Coming up in New York and Harlem theatres
title: Joining Wilbur Sweatman, then George Stevens at Larchmont
summary: He tours New England with clarinetist Wilbur Sweatman, reaches New York in 1921, and plays Larchmont with singer George Stevens before returning to Boston.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Wilbur Sweatman was a clarinet player. He used to play three clarinets at a time, see, and he had a group and he wanted a piano player so they picked me and I went with him. We traveled all over New England and then we come into New York in '21. The last part of '21, we came into New York and a fellow said Tom, I got a job for you, so I
went up to Larchmont, the Washington Arms. George Stevens, that was his name and he had the group. He was a singer. He used to be in the Shuffle Along show, he was a singer, good looking boy.
Yeah, he was a singer with Shuffle Along.
Was Wilbur Sweatman in this band, too.

No, I quit Sweatman see, and went with George Stevens up at Larchmont. And we stayed there about a week or so and the man fired George because all the women were after George, see, and the man didn't want nothing like that, so when he fired George, we all quit and the man says, I didn't -- he said, where you going, and we said you fired us, didn't you.
So I went back to Boston then and hung around Boston and I owed eight months rent.
